clusters.name: Walter's move across the country, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move from Millbrook to Sorrel Valley in March 1952: within months, June's anxiety rose as she wrote daily to her sister back home, she and Walter grew distant as he worked long hours, Glen got into fights at school, Walter cut off from his brother Harlan over their father's land money, June's functioning fell and she kept to her bed through the winter, they rowed over money for new trees, and by September 1953 June's anxiety eased as she joined the church choir and her letters thinned out. The shifts pile up over a year and a half around the move and its upheaval.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failed, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when the frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter began drinking heavily within weeks, he and Glen blamed each other and clashed, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter, you began wetting the bed in April 1969, Ida's heart trouble was found that May, and by October Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees. The shifts in functioning and relationship moves in the family pile up through the crisis and its aftermath.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss in February 1975 when the Ridgeport cannery closed: by May Glen was out of work most of that year and sat in the truck for hours, he and Marian fought loudly at night over money, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, you stopped eating and lost weight that summer, you kept to your room and grew distant from your mother, Walter began drinking again after six years in December, and by June 1976 you were eating again and made the track team. The shifts in functioning and relationship cluster through this year of financial strain in the household.

clusters.name: Wilma moved into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into your house in January 1990 after she sold her farm: within months you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals, you and Sam grew distant as he stayed late at work and kept out of the rows, Sam took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool in June, Wilma took over Lily's care, your eczema flared on both hands in September, you and Sam rowed most nights by November, and by June 1991 when Wilma took a flat in town your eczema cleared over the summer. The shifts in your symptoms and your relationship moves with Sam and with Wilma run through this period of household upheaval.

declined.reason: 1994: The wildfire came over the ridge on 12 August and the family came home by 15 August, safe. All shifts fall within four days around a real threat that soon passed—you were frightened and kept the children in sight, Lily was sick to her stomach in the gym, you and Sam clashed over whether to drive out, Owen would not sleep without a light on—and you were calm again within the week once home. This is an acute episode around a real event, not a period of heightened family process.

1996–1997: Tess's drinking began in October 1996 and Marian began paying her rent and keeping Jesse most weekends by January 1997, but the recount without shifts told as how things always were leaves one shift that counts—Tess stopped drinking and went to meetings twice a week in June 1997—only one shift, so there is not enough in the diagram to choose a reading. Your worry for Tess in November 1996 and the conflict between Tess and Rick in March 1997 do not themselves count as family process changes.
